newsitem.title: USA: FTC ok's pact in Time Warner, Turner merger - WSJ.
newsitem.headline: FTC ok's pact in Time Warner, Turner merger - WSJ.

text.p: The Federal Trade Commission approved a settlement that paves the way for the completion of the $5.6 billion merger between Time Warner Inc and Turner Broadcasting System Inc, the Wall Street Journal reported Thursday.

The vote was 3-2, the article said. Two commissioners cast "no" votes not because they opposed the merger but because they believe the merger did not violate antitrust laws and so did not require a settlement.

The settlement resolves the role of Tele-Communications Inc, which currently owns 21 percent of Turner Broadcasting. TCI's stake in the new company will be limited to 9.2 percent of the voting shares, and it will be held by shareholders of TCI's Liberty Media subsidiary.
TCI Chairman John Malone and the company's controlling shareholders will be prohibited from a management role in the new company, the article said.
An announcement from the FTC is expected Thursday, the article said.
